claim: AWS Directory Service provides multiple ways to use Microsoft Active Directory with other AWS services, with directory choices for existing Microsoft AD or LDAP-aware applications in the cloud.
question: What is AWS Directory Service in one sentence?

values.display: multiple ways to use Microsoft Active Directory (AD)
multiple directory choices for customers

evidence.quote: AWS Directory Service provides multiple ways to use Microsoft Active Directory (AD) with other AWS services.
AWS Directory Service provides multiple directory choices for customers who want to use existing Microsoft AD or Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP)–aware applications in the cloud.

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD is powered by an actual Microsoft Windows Server Active Directory, managed by AWS in the AWS Cloud, and lets you migrate a broad range of Active Directory-aware applications to AWS.
question: Is AWS Managed Microsoft AD real Microsoft Active Directory?

values.display: an actual Microsoft Windows Server Active Directory
managed by AWS in the AWS Cloud

evidence.quote: Also known as AWS Managed Microsoft AD, AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory is powered by an actual Microsoft Windows Server Active Directory (AD), managed by AWS in the AWS Cloud. It enables you to migrate a broad range of Active Directory–aware applications to the AWS Cloud.

claim: Applications that work with AWS Managed Microsoft AD can use user credentials stored in the directory, or the directory can connect with a trust to an existing Active Directory running on premises or on EC2 Windows and use its credentials.
question: Can AWS Managed Microsoft AD use credentials from an on-premises Active Directory?

values.display: with a trust and use credentials
running on-premises or on EC2 Windows

qualifiers.condition: a trust to the existing Active Directory

evidence.quote: All compatible applications work with user credentials that you store in AWS Managed Microsoft AD, or you can [connect to your existing AD infrastructure](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/ms_ad_connect_existing_infrastructure.html) with a trust and use credentials from an Active Directory running on-premises or on EC2 Windows.

claim: On its own, AWS Managed Microsoft AD lets users sign in to the AWS Management Console with Active Directory credentials; together with IAM Identity Center, users can also get short-term credentials for the AWS SDK and CLI and use preconfigured SAML integrations to sign in to many cloud applications.
question: What federated access does AWS Managed Microsoft AD give alone, and what does IAM Identity Center add?

values.display: supports federated use cases using Active Directory credentials
short-term credentials for use with the AWS SDK
preconfigured SAML integrations

evidence.quote: AWS Managed Microsoft AD also supports federated use cases using Active Directory credentials. Alone, AWS Managed Microsoft AD enables you to sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/). With [AWS IAM Identity Center](https://aws.amazon.com/single-sign-on/), you can also obtain short-term credentials for use with the AWS SDK and CLI, and use preconfigured SAML integrations to sign in to many cloud applications.

claim: By adding Microsoft Entra Connect, and optionally AD FS, users can sign in to Microsoft Office 365 and other cloud applications with credentials stored in AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
question: How can users sign in to Microsoft Office 365 with credentials stored in AWS Managed Microsoft AD?

values.display: By adding Microsoft Entra Connect
sign in to Microsoft Office 365

evidence.quote: By adding Microsoft Entra Connect (formerly known as Azure Active Directory Connect), and optionally Active Directory Federation Service (AD FS), you can sign in to Microsoft Office 365 and other cloud applications with credentials stored in AWS Managed Microsoft AD.

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD can enable multi-factor authentication for users who access AWS applications from the internet, and because Active Directory is an LDAP directory it can serve Linux SSH authentication and other LDAP-enabled applications.
question: Does AWS Managed Microsoft AD support MFA and LDAP-based Linux authentication?

values.display: an additional layer of security
Linux Secure Shell (SSH) authentication
Active Directory is an LDAP directory

evidence.quote: You can also [enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) for AWS Managed Microsoft AD](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/ms_ad_mfa.html) to provide an additional layer of security when users access AWS applications from the Internet.
Because Active Directory is an LDAP directory, you can also use AWS Managed Microsoft AD for Linux Secure Shell (SSH) authentication and for other LDAP-enabled applications.

claim: With AWS Managed Microsoft AD, AWS provides monitoring, daily snapshots and recovery as part of the service, while you add users and groups and administer Group Policy with familiar Active Directory tools from a Windows computer joined to the domain.
question: What does AWS manage in AWS Managed Microsoft AD, and what do you still administer?

values.display: monitoring, daily snapshots, and recovery
administer Group Policy using familiar Active Directory tools

evidence.quote: AWS provides monitoring, daily snapshots, and recovery as part of the service—you [add users and groups to AWS Managed Microsoft AD](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/ms_ad_manage_users_groups.html), and administer Group Policy using familiar Active Directory tools running on a Windows computer joined to the AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain.

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD is the best choice when you need actual Active Directory features for AWS applications or Windows workloads (including RDS for SQL Server), a standalone Active Directory in the AWS Cloud that supports Office 365, or an LDAP directory for Linux applications.
question: When is AWS Managed Microsoft AD the best choice among the directory types?

values.display: need actual Active Directory features
a standalone Active Directory in the AWS Cloud
an LDAP directory to support your Linux applications

evidence.quote: AWS Managed Microsoft AD is your best choice if you need actual Active Directory features to support AWS applications or Windows workloads, including Amazon Relational Database Service for Microsoft SQL Server. It's also best if you want a standalone Active Directory in the AWS Cloud that supports Office 365 or you need an LDAP directory to support your Linux applications.

claim: AD Connector is a proxy service that connects compatible AWS applications, such as WorkSpaces, Amazon Quick and EC2 Windows Server instances, to an existing on-premises Microsoft Active Directory; it forwards users' sign-in requests to the on-premises domain controllers for authentication.
question: What is AD Connector and where does authentication happen?

values.display: AD Connector is a proxy service
forwards sign-in requests to your on-premises Active Directory

evidence.quote: AD Connector is a proxy service that provides an easy way to connect compatible AWS applications, such as Amazon WorkSpaces, Amazon Quick, and [Amazon EC2](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/) for Windows Server instances, to your existing on-premises Microsoft Active Directory.
When users log in to the AWS applications, AD Connector forwards sign-in requests to your on-premises Active Directory domain controllers for authentication.

claim: AD Connector removes the need for directory synchronization and for hosting a federation infrastructure; you keep managing users, groups and passwords in the on-premises Active Directory with standard tools.
question: Does AD Connector synchronize the on-premises directory into AWS?

values.display: eliminates the need of directory synchronization
manage your Active Directory as you do now

evidence.quote: AD Connector also eliminates the need of directory synchronization or the cost and complexity of hosting a federation infrastructure.

With AD Connector, you continue to manage your Active Directory as you do now. For example, you add new users and groups and update passwords using standard Active Directory administration tools in your on-premises Active Directory .

claim: AD Connector is not compatible with Amazon RDS for SQL Server.
question: Can Amazon RDS for SQL Server use AD Connector?

values.display: not compatible with RDS SQL Server

evidence.quote: AD Connector is not compatible with RDS SQL Server.

claim: AD Connector lets users access the AWS Management Console with their existing Active Directory credentials, and it can enable MFA for AWS application users by connecting to the existing RADIUS-based MFA infrastructure.
question: Can AD Connector give console access with AD credentials and add MFA?

values.display: access the AWS Management Console
your existing RADIUS-based MFA infrastructure

evidence.quote: AD Connector also allows your users to access the AWS Management Console and manage AWS resources by logging in with their existing Active Directory credentials.

You can also use AD Connector to [enable multi-factor authentication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/ad_connector_mfa.html) (MFA) for your AWS application users by connecting it to your existing RADIUS-based MFA infrastructure.

claim: AD Connector is the best choice when you want to use your existing on-premises directory with compatible AWS services.
question: When is AD Connector the best choice among the directory types?

values.display: use your existing on-premises directory

evidence.quote: AD Connector is your best choice when you want to use your existing on-premises directory with compatible AWS services.

claim: Simple AD is a Microsoft Active Directory-compatible directory powered by Samba 4 that supports basic features such as user accounts, group memberships, domain join of Linux and Windows EC2 instances, Kerberos-based SSO and group policies.
question: What is Simple AD and which Active Directory features does it support?

values.display: powered by Samba 4
Kerberos-based SSO, and group policies

evidence.quote: Simple AD is a Microsoft Active Directory–*compatible* directory from AWS Directory Service that is powered by Samba 4. Simple AD supports basic Active Directory features such as user accounts, group memberships, joining a Linux domain or Windows based EC2 instances, Kerberos-based SSO, and group policies.

claim: Simple AD does not support MFA, trust relationships, DNS dynamic update, schema extensions, LDAPS, PowerShell AD cmdlets or FSMO role transfer, and it is not compatible with RDS SQL Server; customers who need an actual Microsoft Active Directory should use AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
question: Which features does Simple AD not support?

values.display: does not support multi-factor authentication (MFA), trust relationships
schema extensions, communication over LDAPS
Simple AD is not compatible with RDS SQL Server

evidence.quote: Simple AD does not support multi-factor authentication (MFA), trust relationships, DNS dynamic update, schema extensions, communication over LDAPS, PowerShell AD cmdlets, or FSMO role transfer. Simple AD is not compatible with RDS SQL Server. Customers who require the features of an actual Microsoft Active Directory, or who envision using their directory with RDS SQL Server should use AWS Managed Microsoft AD instead.

claim: Simple AD can be used as a standalone directory in the cloud for Windows workloads that need basic Active Directory features, for compatible AWS applications, or for Linux workloads that need an LDAP service.
question: When can Simple AD be used?

values.display: a standalone directory in the cloud
need basic Active Directory features

evidence.quote: You can use Simple AD as a standalone directory in the cloud to support Windows workloads that need basic Active Directory features, compatible AWS applications, or to support Linux workloads that need LDAP service.
